Therefore let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God,
For this reason let us go on from the first things about Christ to full growth; not building again that on which it is based, that is, the turning of the heart from dead works, and faith in God,
所以，我們應當離開基督道理的開端，竭力進到完全的地步，不必再立根基，就如那懊悔死行、信靠神、
instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
The teaching of baptisms, and of the putting on of hands, and of the future life of the dead, and of the judging on the last day.
各樣洗禮、按手之禮、死人復活，以及永遠審判各等教訓。
And this we will do, if God permits.
Now we will do this, if God lets us.
神若許我們，我們必如此行。
It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit,
As for those who at one time saw the light, tasting the good things from heaven, and having their part in the Holy Spirit,
論到那些已經蒙了光照、嘗過天恩的滋味、又於聖靈有分，
who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age—
With knowledge of the good word of God, and of the powers of the coming time,
並嘗過神善道的滋味、覺悟來世權能的人，
and then have fallen away—to be restored to repentance, because they themselves are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.
And then let themselves be turned away, it is not possible for their hearts to be made new a second time; because they themselves put the Son of God on the cross again, openly shaming him.
若是離棄道理，就不能叫他們重新懊悔了。因為他們把神的兒子重釘十字架，明明地羞辱他。
For land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended receives the blessing of God.
For a land, drinking in the frequent rain and producing good plants for those for whom it is worked, has a blessing from God:
就如一塊田地，吃過屢次下的雨水，生長菜蔬，合乎耕種的人用，就從神得福；
But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. In the end it will be burned.
But if it sends up thorns and evil plants, it is of no use and is ready to be cursed; its only end is to be burned.
若長荊棘和蒺藜，必被廢棄，近於咒詛，結局就是焚燒。
Even though we speak like this, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case—things that accompany salvation.
But, my loved ones, though we say this, we are certain that you have better things in you, things which go with salvation;
親愛的弟兄們，我們雖是這樣說，卻深信你們的行為強過這些，而且近乎得救。
For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.
For God is true, and will not put away from him the memory of your work and of your love for his name, in the help which you gave and still give to the saints.
因為神並非不公義，竟忘記你們所做的工和你們為他名所顯的愛心，就是先前伺候聖徒，如今還是伺候。
We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.
And it is our desire that you may all keep the same high purpose in certain hope to the end:
我們願你們各人都顯出這樣的殷勤，使你們有滿足的指望，一直到底。
Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised.
So that you may not be slow in heart, but may take as your example those to whom God has given their heritage, because of their faith and their long waiting.
並且不懈怠，總要效法那些憑信心和忍耐承受應許的人。
When God made His promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself,
For when God made his oath to Abraham, because there was no greater oath, he made it by himself,
當初神應許亞伯拉罕的時候，因為沒有比自己更大可以指著起誓的，就指著自己起誓，說：
saying, “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants.”
Saying, Be certain that I will give you my blessing, and make your numbers very great.
「論福，我必賜大福給你；論子孫，我必叫你的子孫多起來。」
And so Abraham, after waiting patiently, obtained the promise.
And so, when he had been waiting calmly for a long time, God's word to him was put into effect.
這樣，亞伯拉罕既恆久忍耐，就得了所應許的。
Men swear by someone greater than themselves, and their oath serves as a confirmation to end all argument.
For men at all times make their oaths by what is greater; and any argument is ended by the decision of the oath.
人都是指著比自己大的起誓，並且以起誓為實據，了結各樣的爭論。
So when God wanted to make the unchanging nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise, He guaranteed it with an oath.
So that when it was God's desire to make it specially clear to those who by his word were to have the heritage, that his purpose was fixed, he made it more certain with an oath;
照樣，神願意為那承受應許的人格外顯明他的旨意是不更改的，就起誓為證。
Thus by two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged.
So that we, who have gone in flight from danger to the hope which has been put before us, may have a strong comfort in two unchanging things, in which it is not possible for God to be false;
藉這兩件不更改的事，神決不能說謊，好叫我們這逃往避難所、持定擺在我們前頭指望的人可以大得勉勵。
We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,
And this hope is like a strong band for our souls, fixed and certain, and going in to that which is inside the veil;
我們有這指望，如同靈魂的錨，又堅固又牢靠，且通入幔內。
where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf. He has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
Where Jesus has gone before us, as a high priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.
作先鋒的耶穌，既照著麥基洗德的等次成了永遠的大祭司，就為我們進入幔內。
